_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Uninhabited Island and Early Sightings
910.label: Event
910.description: Volcanic island in the Indian Ocean; no indigenous human population; Arab and Portuguese sailors sight the island before Dutch arrival.

910.name: Volcanic Formation and Endemic Species
910.label: Event
910.description: Mauritius formed by volcanic activity ~10 million years ago; evolution of unique endemic species including the dodo, giant tortoises, and native flora.

910.name: Arab and Portuguese Sightings
910.label: Event
910.description: Arab navigators possibly map the island (Dina Arobi); Portuguese chart it as Cerne (c. 1507); no permanent settlement established.

920.name: Dutch Colonial Period
920.label: Event
920.description: Dutch East India Company names island after Prince Maurits; ebony exploitation; introduction of sugar cane; dodo driven to extinction; Dutch abandon island.

920.name: Dutch Settlement and Exploitation
920.label: Event
920.description: Admiral Wybrand van Warwyck claims island 1598; named Mauritius after Prince Maurits of Nassau; ebony forests logged; enslaved workers from Madagascar.

920.name: Extinction of the Dodo
920.label: Event
920.description: Flightless dodo (Raphus cucullatus) driven to extinction by hunting, introduced predators, and habitat destruction; last sighting c. 1681.

930.name: French Colonial Period (Île de France)
930.label: Event
930.description: France colonises island as Île de France; sugar plantation economy; slave-based labour; corsair base; Mahé de La Bourdonnais as governor.

930.name: Foundation of Île de France
930.label: Event
930.description: French East India Company claims island 1715; renamed Île de France; Mahé de La Bourdonnais as governor from 1735 transforms the colony.

930.name: Sugar Plantations and Slavery
930.label: Event
930.description: Sugar cane becomes dominant crop; enslaved people from East Africa, Madagascar, and India; code noir; Maroon communities.

940.name: British Colonial Mauritius
940.label: Event
940.description: British capture and Treaty of Paris; abolition of slavery; Indian indentured labour transforms demographics; sugar monoculture; path to independence.

940.name: British Takeover and Abolition
940.label: Event
940.description: Britain captures Mauritius 1810; Treaty of Paris 1814; French laws and language retained; abolition of slavery 1835; apprenticeship system.

940.name: Indian Indentured Labour System
940.label: Event
940.description: Over 450,000 Indian indentured labourers brought to sugar plantations (Aapravasi Ghat, UNESCO site); transforms ethnic composition; 'coolie trade' abuses.

950.name: Independence and Nation-Building
950.label: Event
950.description: Independence 1968 amid ethnic tensions; Chagos Archipelago detached; Ramgoolam and Jugnauth era; economic diversification begins.

950.name: Independence of Mauritius
950.label: Event
950.description: Independence 12 March 1968; Seewoosagur Ramgoolam as first PM; ethnic riots precede independence; Chagos Archipelago (incl. Diego Garcia) detached by Britain.

950.name: Chagos Archipelago Detachment
950.label: Event
950.description: Britain separates Chagos from Mauritius 1965 (BIOT); Chagossian population expelled for Diego Garcia US base; ICJ 2019 advisory opinion supports Mauritius sovereignty.

960.name: Mauritian Economic Miracle
960.label: Event
960.description: Republic since 1992; transformation into financial services, ICT, and tourism hub; highest HDI in Africa; multicultural democracy.

960.name: Republic of Mauritius
960.label: Event
960.description: Mauritius becomes a republic within the Commonwealth 1992; Cassam Uteem as first president; parliamentary democracy continues.

960.name: Financial Services and ICT Hub
960.label: Event
960.description: Global Business Licence regime; Mauritius as India-Africa investment gateway; Cybercity Ebène; diversified services economy.
